chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Yaqoub ibn Shuayb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he (peace be upon him) was saying:
O the One Who is grateful for the little, and pardons the much, and He is the Forgiving, the Merciful. Forgive me the sins whose pleasure has passed and whose consequence remains.

key_terms.يَشْكُرُ الْيَسِيرَ: He is grateful for the little (small deeds)

ai.seo_question: What is the supplication for sins whose pleasure has passed but consequences remain?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) articulates a profound psychological insight into repentance, distinguishing between the transient pleasure of sin and its enduring spiritual burden, thereby encouraging sincere remorse. This supplication is frequently recited in Shia tradition as a comprehensive means of seeking forgiveness, emphasizing Allah's attribute of 'Al-Ghafur Al-Rahim' (The All-Forgiving, The Merciful) in response to human frailty. It reflects the Shia emphasis on the balance between hope in divine mercy and awareness of the lasting consequences of disobedience.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Yaqoub Bin Shuayb, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, that he<sup>asws</sup> was saying:

‘O the One Who Thanks for the less, and Forgives from the more, and He<sup>azwj</sup> is the Forgiving, the Merciful. Forgive my sins for me whose pleasure has (already) gone, and there remains its consequence’’.
en.sarwar: 28. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ya’qub ibn Shu’ayb from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
O the One who appreciates the very little and pardons a great deal, who is forgiving and merciful, forgive my sins, the pleasures of which are gone and the consequences have remained.”
